findings.title: settings-defaults.test.ts uses SETTING_ENUMS, a constant the schema never declares
findings.section: Task 4 (settings schema Produces at line 1511; Step 6 defaults test import at 1985, use at 2019) and Task 6 (consumes SETTING_OPTION_VALUES at 2953/3228).
findings.whats_wrong: An implementer typing Task 4 Step 6's test verbatim cannot compile it: it imports SETTING_ENUMS from ./settings-schema and does `SETTING_ENUMS[path]?.[shipped as string]`, but the schema's Produces declares only SETTING_OPTION_VALUES (`Record<string, readonly string[]>`) — SETTING_ENUMS is never declared/exported anywhere (grep = 2 hits, both in the test). TWO PROPOSED FIXES CONFLICTED and verify RESOLVED it: coherence proposed renaming SETTING_ENUMS -> SETTING_OPTION_VALUES, but verify proved that is WRONG on two counts — it fails typecheck (TS7053: a string[] cannot be indexed by a string key) AND fails semantically (indexing a name[] by a name yields undefined, so `expected` becomes the enum NAME while the test compares it to a NUMBER). Feasibility's fix is correct: SETTING_ENUMS is a DISTINCT missing constant that resolves an enum NAME to its NUMBER, which SETTING_OPTION_VALUES cannot do. Bonus gap verify found: the drift test the schema promises ('asserts this map equals every option list buildSettingGroups(engine) produces', lines 1507-09) is never actually written.
findings.why_it_works: The test resolves an enum name to its numeric value (`SETTING_ENUMS[path]?.[name] -> number`, then `?? shipped` for non-enum rows). SETTING_OPTION_VALUES holds the names as string arrays but not their numbers, so it genuinely cannot serve; SETTING_ENUMS and SETTING_OPTION_VALUES are two distinct constants with different shapes and purposes (one converts names->numbers in the defaults test, the other gates stored values in Task 6). Writing the promised drift test closes the second, independent gap: without it, if SETTING_OPTION_VALUES drifts from the real option lists, Task 6's dropUnknownOptions silently wipes valid stored enum values and raises a false 'settings were reset' toast.
evidence: export const SETTING_OPTION_VALUES: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>>;
import { DEFAULT_PLAYER_SETTINGS, SETTING_ENUMS } from './settings-schema';
const expected = SETTING_ENUMS[path]?.[shipped as string] ?? shipped;
it asserts this map equals every option list buildSettingGroups(engine)
findings.verify: REAL conflict between the two proposed fixes; Fix B (add distinct SETTING_ENUMS name->number map) WINS. Fix A (rename) fails typecheck (TS7053) AND semantics (yields a name, test needs a number). Undeclared SETTING_ENUMS confirmed (grep = 2 hits, both in the test). Promised drift test confirmed unwritten. NOTE: this is precisely the finding the engine would have silently mis-applied as coherence's safe_auto rename — do not apply the rename.

findings.whats_wrong: The Global Constraints bullet explains why to key on aria-expanded using a 'stacked trigger' construction as the reason — but lap-3's F-10 retired the stacked trigger in favour of the span-wrap (a TooltipTrigger rendering a <span> AROUND a PopoverTrigger), which the plan now uses at lines 2651 and 3707. findings.before:

- **`data-popup-open` cannot tell a tooltip from a popover.** Both triggers map their open state to the same attribute (`utils/popupStateMapping.js:45`), so on the stacked trigger it is present on hover as well as when the popover is open. The discriminator is `aria-expanded`; never key a style or an assertion on `data-popup-open` for either trigger.
findings.after:

findings.title: Player-mode's two dead-end options carry no inline warning
findings.section: Task 8 Step 1 schema entry (lines 3877-3896; the two dead options at 3890-3891). SettingRow description support in Task 2 (lines 409/841).
findings.whats_wrong: Picking 'An external media player' or 'No playback' from the player-mode dropdown silently disables the whole transport, and the only explanation lives on the Play button's tooltip elsewhere in the header — not near the control the person just used. SettingRow's `description` field exists for exactly this kind of caveat (every stylesheet row carries one), but the player-mode row's schema entry uses none. Nothing is unrecoverable (Settings is never disabled), which is why this is advisory polish, not a blocking gap.
